identity.name: Potassium benzoate
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salt of benzoic acid (aromatic carboxylate preservative)

function.mechanism: Weak-acid benzoate preservative system; antimicrobial effect is strongest in acidic foods where the benzoic acid form can inhibit microbial growth.

adi.basis: Group ADI for benzoic acid and benzoates (E210-E213), expressed as benzoic acid

efsa.key_finding: EFSA's 2016 re-evaluation maintained the group ADI but reported high-percentile exposure exceedance in younger groups under some scenarios.

fda.notes: eCFR API shows potassium benzoate in indirect food-contact use (closure-sealing gaskets) at 1% limit; no standalone direct-food GRAS section for potassium benzoate was identified in 21 CFR part 184.

adi.basis: JECFA 2021 group ADI 0-20 mg/kg bw, expressed as benzoic acid equivalents, replacing previous 0-5 mg/kg bw

concerns.summary: A human-lymphocyte in vitro study reported increased chromosomal aberrations, micronuclei, and comet-assay DNA damage for potassium benzoate and sodium benzoate at tested concentrations.
Rodent data with benzoate preservatives (mainly sodium benzoate) reported oxidative-stress and learning/memory effects, but direct transfer to potassium-benzoate dietary risk remains uncertain.
Recent review and computational literature continue to flag possible cytogenotoxic concerns for common preservatives, including benzoates, but evidence quality is heterogeneous and often indirect.

no_concern_confirmed: No IARC Group 1/2A/2B classification identified for potassium benzoate in the current IARC list dataset.
A randomized trial in children found no significant adverse behavioral effect for sodium benzoate alone in that study design.
JECFA increased the benzoate group ADI to 0-20 mg/kg bw in 2021.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA re-evaluation reported high-percentile benzoate exposures above the EU group ADI (5 mg/kg bw/day) in some younger population groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Potassium benzoate remains regulated and not IARC-classified, but EFSA identified high-consumer ADI exceedance in children for benzoates and there are credible in vitro/mechanistic safety signals that justify a moderate-caution tier rather than limited-risk.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 5 mg/kg bw/day with high-percentile exceedance in younger groups
FDA CFR citation found for indirect food-contact use (21 CFR 177.1210) with explicit limit
JECFA 2021 group ADI updated to 0-20 mg/kg bw
No IARC listing/classification for potassium benzoate
Potassium-benzoate genotoxicity signal reported in human-lymphocyte in vitro testing
